A note on citation form. MSDH rule citations below give the rule number as printed in S-1 (e.g. "Rule 5.4.6"). S-1's blackline text frequently prints a struck-through old number beside the new number; only the operative (non-struck) number is cited. MDOR citations give Part XI chapter and paragraph (e.g. "35.XI.11 ¶103"). Statute citations give the Miss. Code section. Verbatim quotes are in quotation marks; paraphrase is not quoted.

No personal phone numbers or personal email addresses appear in this file. Agency contact pages that list a general programme mailbox or phone number were not reproduced, except that MDAC's general programme email was deliberately omitted here as well; the MDAC page (S-7) is cited by URL only.

11.1 TESTING

11.1.1 Medical — what must be tested, and when: the governing rule

MSDH Rule 5.4.1 (S-1, Subpart 5) is the operative testing mandate. Its structure:

"A cultivation facility or processing facility shall test [e]very harvest batch of usable medical cannabis flower … prior to selling or transferring the usable medical cannabis" — Rule 5.4.1(B); and "Every production batch of raw pre-rolls shall be tested in [its] the final form intended for sale or distribution" — Rule 5.4.1(C); and every "process lot production batch of cannabinoid concentrate, and extract or edible" shall be tested "in [its] the final form intended for sale or distribution to a qualified patient or caregiver … prior to sale or transfer" — Rule 5.4.1(D); and every production batch of infused products, of kief, and of infused pre-rolls and inhalable compound concentrate products likewise in final form prior to sale or transfer — Rule 5.4.1(E)–(G).

Two timing rules cut across all of that:

  • Usable cannabis is sampled only after curing, unless it is intended for sale/transfer to make a cannabinoid concentrate or extract — Rule 5.3.1: "Usable medical cannabis may only be sampled only after it is cured, unless the usable medical cannabis is intended for sale or transfer to a medical cannabis establishment to make a cannabinoid concentrate or extract."
  • Retail-ready product is sampled and tested in final form — Rule 5.3.1: "Retail-ready cannabis products shall be sampled and tested in final form in accordance with the rules in this Part." And: "An employee of a licensed testing facility will obtain and analyze test samples only from usable medical cannabis."
  • No release before passing results are in the system — Rule 5.7.3: "Passed test results must [shall] be in the Department's seed-to-sale system for a batch to be released for immediate processing, packaging, and labeling for transfer or sale in accordance with these Rules." Quarantine pending results is at Rule 5.3.10(L) (see §11.1.4).

11.1.2 Medical — required tests by product type

The eight-test core is identical for flower, raw pre-rolls, concentrates/extracts/edibles, kief and infused pre-rolls/inhalable concentrates, with the additions and exemptions noted below. The table reproduces Rule 5.4.1(B)–(G) as read.

Test (MSDH rule) Flower — every harvest batch (5.4.1(B)) Raw pre-rolls — every production batch, final form (5.4.1(C)) Concentrate / extract / edible — every production batch, final form (5.4.1(D)) Infused products — every production batch, final form (5.4.1(E)) Kief — every production batch, final form (5.4.1(F)) Infused pre-rolls & inhalable compound concentrates — every production batch, final form (5.4.1(G))
Pesticides — Rule 5.4.3 Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes
Water activity & moisture content — Rule 5.4.5 Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes
THC & CBD concentration (potency) — Rule 5.4.6 Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes
Heavy metals — Rule 5.4.7 Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes
Mycotoxins — Rule 5.4.8 Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes
Microbiological contaminants — Rule 5.4.2 Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes
Terpenes — Rule 5.4.9, if performed If performed If performed If performed If performed If performed If performed
Foreign material — Rule 5.4.10 Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes Yes
Solvents — Rule 5.4.4 Not listed in 5.4.1(B) for flower Not listed in 5.4.1(C) Exempt only on the conditions in 5.4.1(D)(9) (see below) Not listed as a separate line in 5.4.1(E) Not listed in 5.4.1(F) Not listed in 5.4.1(G)
Homogeneity — Rule 5.4.11 No No No Yes — 5.4.1(E)(9) No No

Solvent-testing exemption (concentrates) — Rule 5.4.1(D)(9), verbatim in substance:

"A cultivation facility or processing facility entity is exempt from testing concentrates for solvents under this Rule if the cultivation facility or processing facility entity: a. Did not use any solvent listed in Appendix A, Table 2 [Table 1 as blacklined]; and, b. [Used] a mechanical extraction process to separate cannabinoids from the cannabis; or c. Used only water, animal fat or vegetable oil as a solvent to separate the cannabinoids from the cannabis."

Edible-specific additions — Rule 5.4.1(E)(10):

"Final form edible cannabis products shall meet the following additional requirements: a. Produced and sold with a standardized concentration of cannabinoids not to exceed ten milligrams (10 mg) of total tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) per serving with an allowable variance of ±10% when testing. b. Must demonstrate uniform disbursement of cannabinoids throughout the product when sampled and tested."

Water-activity / moisture exemptions — Rule 5.4.1(E)(11): "Infused non-edible products and beverages are exempt from water activity and moisture content testing." That sits alongside Rule 5.4.5(D): "Non-edible infused products are not subject to water activity testing."

Testing standards (pass/fail thresholds) — Rules 5.4.2–5.4.11, verbatim thresholds:

  • Microbiological contaminants (Rule 5.4.2(C)) — a product passes only if all of: (1) "Total Escherichia coli coliform is not detected above 100 colony forming units/gram"; (2) "Shiga toxin–producing Escherichia coli is not detected in 1 gram"; (3) "Salmonella spp. is not detected in 1 gram"; (4) "Pathogenic Aspergillus species A. fumigatus, A. flavus, A. niger, and A. terreus are not detected in 1 gram"; (5) "Total Yeast and Mold is not detected above 10,000 colony-forming units/gram." For non-inhalable products, Rule 5.4.2(D) gives a narrower pass test: total E. coli ≤100 CFU/g, Shiga toxin–producing E. coli not detected in 1 g, and Salmonella spp. not detected in 1 g. Failure consequence: "If the sample fails microbial impurities testing, the batch from which the sample was collected fails microbial impurities testing and shall not be released for retail sale" — Rule 5.4.2(E).
  • Pesticides (Rule 5.4.3): tested by a licensed testing facility "approved for the analytes listed in Appendix A, Table 1"; the facility "shall report whether any Residual Pesticides are detected above the limit of detection (LOD) and shall report the result of the testing in ppms on the Certificate of Analysis" and indicate "pass" or "fail". A batch fails if a pesticide is detected "above the action levels listed in Appendix A, Table 1" on initial test (no reanalysis requested) or on reanalysis under Rule 5.5.1. Appendix A action levels themselves were not reproduced in the rendered text read for this file [VERIFY] — the numeric pesticide action levels must be taken from Appendix A of the current Part 22 filing, not from this summary.
  • Solvents (Rule 5.4.4): reported in ppm on the COA with "pass"/"fail". A batch fails if a solvent is detected above the Appendix A, Table 2 [Table 1] action level, or if the lab "[c]alculates a RPD of more than twenty percent (20%) between the field primary result of the sample and the field duplicate result."
  • Water activity / moisture (Rule 5.4.5): "If a sample has a water activity rate of more than 0.65 aw the sample fails except for an edible infused cannabis product"; an edible infused product fails if water activity is "more than 0.85 aw"; "If a sample has a moisture content of more than fifteen percent (15%), the sample fails."
  • Potency (Rule 5.4.6): the lab must test, at minimum and "without any corrective factor taken for moisture content": Delta-8-THC; Delta-8-THCA; Delta-9-THC; Delta-9-THCA; CBD; CBDA; THC content; CBN; and "any other cannabinoid determined by the department". Limit of quantitation "1.0 mg/g or lower for all cannabinoids analyzed and reported". The COA must give dry-weight percent (formula: dry-weight percent = wet-weight percent / (1 − percent moisture/100)), total THC and total CBD percentages, mg/g or mg/mL, mg/package, and mg/serving where applicable. Potency caps — Rule 5.4.6(E)(12): "The sample shall be deemed to have passed the cannabinoid testing if the amount of THC does not exceed the limits below: a. Cannabis flower or trim potency ≤ 30% total THC; b. Cannabis tinctures, oils or concentrates ≤ 60% total THC." This confirms the Run 1 caps. Label tolerance: "Total THC, and/or Total CBD claimed to be present on a label shall not be considered inaccurate if the difference in percentage on the certificate of analysis is plus or minus 10.0%" — Rule 5.4.6(G). Potency homogeneity for concentrates: a process-lot production batch fails potency if, on initial test or reanalysis, the THC amount between samples from the batch exceeds the stated RSD limit — the blackline text prints "thirty twenty percent (320%) RSD"; the operative figure is [VERIFY] because the rendered blackline is ambiguous between 30% and 20%. Do not quote either figure as settled until the clean current rule is checked.
  • Heavy metals (Rule 5.4.7): tested for "the metals listed in Appendix A"; reported on the COA with "pass"/"fail"; a batch fails if metals are detected "above the action level listed in Appendix A, Table 3 [Table 1]". The metal-by-metal action levels were not reproduced in the text read [VERIFY — Appendix A].
  • Mycotoxins (Rule 5.4.8): tested for "Aflatoxin B1, B2, G1, and G2 [and] Ochratoxin A". Pass requires: "Total of aflatoxin B1, B2, G1, and G2 does not exceed 20 µg/kg of substance, and … Ochratoxin A does not exceed 20 µg/kg of substance."
  • Terpenoids (Rule 5.4.9): "Terpene analysis is not required. However, if terpene content is listed on product packaging or label, a terpene analysis … must [shall] be performed to confirm the product label." Label tolerance ±10.0% per terpenoid claimed.
  • Foreign material (Rule 5.4.10): tested on "the total representative sample prior to sample homogenization"; the lab must "[e]xamine both the exterior and interior of the dried flower sample" and "[e]xamine the exterior of the cannabis product sample". Pass if foreign material does not exceed: "One-fourth (1/4) of the total sample area covered by sand, soil, cinders, or dirt"; 1/4 covered by mold; "One (1) insect fragment, 1 hair, or 1 count mammalian excreta per 3.0 grams"; or 1/4 covered by an embedded foreign material. Failure: "the batch … fails foreign material testing and shall not be released for retail sale."
  • Homogeneity (Rule 5.4.11): "Infused cannabis products must be homogenous, with the THC and CBD content evenly distributed throughout"; a product is homogeneous only if "the concentration of total THC and/or CBD in milligrams per serving for three (3) units from the batch is +/- 15% of the stated THC/CBD per serving"; "Each type of infused product shall be tested every six (6) months and any time the manufacturing process or ingredient(s) change"; a product that fails "shall not be released for retail sale" and "[a]ll subsequent production batches of the failed item type shall undergo homogeneity testing until three (3) consecutive batches pass."
  • Summary appendices: "All compliance testing requirements by product type are summarized in Appendix D and all compliance testing requirements by final packaging are summarized in Appendix E" — Rule 5.4.1(H). Appendices D and E were not reproduced in the rendered text read [VERIFY].
  • R&D testing (Rule 5.4.13): permitted only before compliance testing for all analytes except terpenes (which "shall always be ordered as an R&D test"); must be "fully completed and reported into the seed-to-sale system … BEFORE the final compliance testing can be ordered"; "shall not replace the Department's required safety compliance testing"; and "[p]unitive action shall not be taken against a licensed medical cannabis establishment for conducting research and development testing when permitted."

Result-entry deadline (all tests): "The testing entity shall enter all test results into the seed-to-sale system within three (3) business days of test completion" — Rules 5.4.2(G), 5.4.5(G), 5.4.6(I), 5.4.7(D), 5.4.8(E), 5.4.9(E), 5.4.10(G), 5.4.11(H). For remediated batches the deadline is tighter: "Within one (1) business day of completing the required analyses of a representative sample obtained from a remediated cannabis or cannabis product batch, the cannabis testing facility entity shall upload the COA information into the seed-to-sale system" — Rule 5.5.9(E).

11.1.3 Medical — testing facility licensing and requirements

Licensing agency and independence. Cannabis testing facilities are licensed and registered by MSDH (Miss. Code § 41-137-35(1), via S-10). The MSDH definition (Rule 1.2.28) is:

"Cannabis Testing Facility Entity … means an independent entity licensed and registered by the Mississippi Department of Health that analyzes the safety and potency of cannabis."

Independence is policed on change of ownership: every owner of a testing facility must attest, signed and dated, that the owner "does not have a direct or indirect familial or financial relationship with or interest in a dispensary, cannabis cultivation facility entity, cannabis processing facility entity, cannabis dispensary, cannabis transportation entity, cannabis disposal entity or cannabis research facility entity" and "pledging not to divert cannabis to any individual or entity that is not allowed to possess cannabis" — Rule 3.10.4(E)(2)–(3). The change-of-ownership application for a testing facility must also carry the entity's legal name, each principal officer and board member, an attestation of truth, signatures of the owners and the technical laboratory director with dates, per-owner no-excluded-felony attestations, and verification that each principal officer/board member is at least 21 — Rule 3.10.4(A)–(F).

Scope of licence. "Cannabis testing facilities entities shall test for cannabis-related analytes for which they are licensed and registered by the Department" — Rule 5.1.1. If a testing facility "is not accredited for the full scope of state-required tests, the testing facility will need to subcontract with another Department-licensed testing facility for the relevant tests needed. All subcontracted testing must [shall] be documented in the seed-to-sale system and be transferred using appropriate transport processes and chain of custody" — Rule 5.4.12.

Accreditation. The Part 22 definitions anchor accreditation to ISO/IEC 17025:2017 (Rule 1.2.1: "being currently deemed as technically competent under ISO/IEC 17025:2017 by an international mutual recognition arrangement signatory that has been found to meet ISO/IEC 17011"). Whether ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation is a precondition to initial licensure, or a scope condition that can be satisfied by subcontracting, is not stated in a single sentence in the passages read — Rule 5.4.12 presupposes a facility may lack accreditation "for the full scope", which implies partial accreditation plus subcontracting is contemplated. The initial-licence accreditation requirement, and any deadline to achieve full accreditation, are therefore [VERIFY] against the current testing-facility licence application and any MSDH testing-facility guidance. Do not assert a blanket "must be ISO 17025-accredited before licensing" on the basis of this file.

Personnel, training, QA and audit — Rules 5.1.2, 5.10, 5.17:

  • "Cannabis testing facilities entities shall develop and implement an employee training program to ensure competency of cannabis testing facility entity employees for their assigned function and shall document each employee's qualifications" — Rule 5.1.2.
  • A written Quality Assurance programme and QA manual are mandatory, covering at minimum: QC procedures; organisation and employee training/responsibilities including good laboratory practice; QA objectives; traceability; instrument maintenance/calibration; performance and system audits; corrective action; process-change steps; record retention/document control; test-procedure standardisation; method validation; chain-of-custody protocols; premise and sample security; sample handling (receipt, identification, rejection, storage, destruction); contingency plans for out-of-control data; and disposal of cannabis and laboratory waste — Rule 5.10.1(A)–(P). The supervisory/management employee must annually review, amend if necessary, and approve the QA programme/manual on creation and on any change in methods, equipment, or supervisory/management employee — Rule 5.10.2.
  • Method SOPs must contain the 16 elements in Rule 5.10.3 (method name, analytes, matrices, receipt/acceptance, sensitivity, interferences, instruments, consumables/reagents/standards, preservation/hold time, QC type/frequency/criteria, calibration type/frequency/criteria, batch procedures, data-quality assessment, calibration of results, reagent/reference preparation, step-by-step instructions).
  • Equipment calibration/maintenance is prescribed in detail at Rule 5.10.5 (daily NIST-certified temperature trending, monthly autoclave bioindicators, quarterly pipette checks / annual calibration, daily balance checks / annual recalibration, annual biosafety-cabinet certification, etc.); service records must be kept "for the life of equipment" — Rule 5.10.5(W).
  • Methods must, to the extent practicable, conform to FDA's Bacteriological Analytical Manual (2019) and AOAC Official Methods of Analysis (21st ed., 2019), and be validated per AOAC Appendices J and K — Rule 5.10.6 (editions incorporated by reference, "includes no future editions or amendments").
  • Analytical-batch QC (Rule 5.11.5, chemistry): QC samples bracketing, following the first 20 samples, every 20 samples thereafter, and at end of testing; initial calibration R² ≥ 0.990, curve recovery ±20% (±30% for the lowest point); continuing calibration verification each analytical batch; at least one each of method blank, laboratory control sample, matrix spike, duplicate matrix spike, and duplicate sample per analytical batch.
  • Internal audit and third-party audit: the testing facility must conduct internal audits per ISO/IEC 17025 standards and submit results to the Department "[w]ithin three (3) business days of completing the internal audit" — Rules 5.17.2–5.17.3; must "contract with an independent, third-party auditor certified to conduct on-site audits at least annually or in accordance with ISO/IEC 17025 accrediting body's requirements" — Rule 5.17.4; must submit the accrediting-body on-site audit report to the Department "[w]ithin three (3) business days of receiving" it — Rule 5.17.5; the Department "reserves the rights to perform additional audits as needed and without advance notice" — Rule 5.17.6.
  • Random compliance checks: "A laboratory testing entity shall comply with random compliance checks at the request of the [Department]. The [Department] or its authorized agents may collect a random sample of a medical cannabis product from a testing facility entity or designate another testing facility entity to collect a random sample … to test that sample for compliance" — Rule 5.4.15.
  • Falsification sanction: "The [Department] shall take immediate disciplinary action, including sanctions, fines, or both, against any laboratory testing entity that falsifies records or [fails] to comply with the provisions of this [Part]" — Rule 5.4.14.
  • Record retention: "A laboratory testing entity must [shall] maintain the documentation required in these rules for at least five years and must [shall] provide that information to the Department upon request" — Rule 5.3.12. Reserve samples: retained "at minimum, for 45 business days after the analyses, after which time it may be destroyed and denatured to the point the material is rendered unrecognizable and unusable"; securely stored "in a manner that prohibits sample degradation, contamination, and tampering"; and "provide[d] … to the Department upon request" — Rules 5.8.1–5.8.3.
  • Testing-facility security carve-out: licensed testing entities are exempt from the fencing requirement in Rule 4.4.4(C) ("Licensed testing entities are exempt from this requirement"). No broader testing-facility security exemption was located; the general Subpart 4 security rules are treated as applying unless a specific exemption states otherwise [VERIFY for processing/testing premises details].

What was NOT located for testing-facility licensing [VERIFY]: a standalone testing-facility initial-application checklist (fees, premises, equipment list, director qualifications beyond the "technical laboratory director" signature in Rule 3.10.4) in the consolidated text read. The general MSDH licensing subpart (Subpart 3) and Subpart 5 QA provisions are the authorities cited above; any testing-specific application form or fee schedule must be checked with MSDH directly.

11.1.4 Medical — sampling rules: who samples, sample size, batch/lot, chain of custody

Who samples. Only the testing facility's own qualified people:

"Only qualified employees/representatives of a licensed testing entity … may take collect and transport test samples and must [shall] follow the testing facility entity's accredited sampling and transportation policies and procedure when collecting samples for testing" — Rule 5.3.10. And: "Qualified [e]mployees/agents of a licensed cannabis testing facility entity are responsible for the collection and transportation of testing samples. Only qualified employees of a licensed cannabis testing entity shall collect and transport medical cannabis test samples" — Rule 5.9.1.

The establishment being sampled may not help: "No employee of the medical cannabis establishment from which a test sample is being collected shall assist the testing facility employee nor touch the harvest and/or production batch package or sampling equipment while the testing facility employee is obtaining the test sample" — Rule 5.3.10(I). But a facility employee "shall be physically present to observe the testing facility employee collect the test sample and ensure that the sample increments are taken from throughout the batch" — Rule 5.3.10(H).

Where sampling happens. "Sampling must [shall] be conducted on-site at a [the] cannabis cultivation facility or [dispensary] processing entity's premises. The testing facility entity personnel shall have access to the entire batch for the purposes of sampling" — Rule 5.3.2. Sampling must be video-recorded (see below).

Batch / lot definitions.

  • "Batch" (Rule 1.2.12): for usable cannabis, "a homogenous, identified quantity of usable medical cannabis, no greater than twenty-five pounds (25 lbs), that is harvested during a specified time period from a specified cultivation area"; for oils, vapours and waxes, "an identified quantity that is uniform, that is intended to meet specifications for identity, strength, and composition, and that is [produced], packaged and labeled during a specified time period according to a single manufacturing, packaging and labeling protocol."
  • Batch number (Rule 1.2.13): "a unique numeric or alphanumeric identifier assigned to a batch by a cultivation or processing facility entity when the batch is first planted. The batch number for plant batches shall contain the strain name and date created. The batch number for harvest batches shall contain the strain name and date harvested. The batch number for production batches shall contain the item name and date produced." Same-date duplicates get a unique suffix.
  • Harvest-batch cap and splitting (Rule 5.2.1): "A medical cannabis establishment must [shall] separate each harvest batch lot of usable medical cannabis into no larger than twenty-five pound (25 lb) batches harvest batch packages for testing purposes."
  • Combining lots (Rule 5.2.2, narrow exception): harvest batches/packages may be combined for sampling only if each batch is intended for a licensed processing entity to make a cannabinoid concentrate or extract and each harvest lot was (A) cultivated with the same growing practices and grown in close proximity on the licensed premises, (B) harvested at the same time, and (C) if cured before sampling, cured under uniform conditions. Combined batches must be labelled to identify the different harvest lots combined. Conversely (Rule 5.2.3): "A medical cannabis establishment may not combine harvest lots into a batch packages for purposes of sampling and testing for THC or CBD." For concentrates/extracts, "a process lot is considered a batch" — Rule 5.2.3, final sentence.
  • Production batch (Rule 1.2.111): "a specifically identifiable quantity of cannabis products … that are processed in one production cycle using either the same extraction methods, manufacturing methods, or formula and the same standard operating procedures", created anew each time a product changes form physically or chemically, changes item category, combines item categories, or has an additive/lipid/flavour/terpene added. A new production batch "requires a new set of compliance tests in final form."
  • Plant batch (Rule 1.2.107): "a batch of identical immature plants logged into the seed-to-sale system as a group on the date received as clones or planted, whichever is earliest, and prior to maturing to the vegetative phase of growth."
  • Batch-number record duty (Rule 5.2.4): each harvest and production batch number must be (A) documented and maintained in the cultivation facility's or dispensary licensee's records "for at least two years and available to the Department upon request", (B) provided to the individual taking testing samples, and (C) included on the batch label.

Sample size — Rules 5.3.4–5.3.8 (all minima; "additional increments may be collected" to ensure representativeness):

Matrix General floor Increment size Batch-size scale (minimum increments / units)
Harvest batch (flower) — Rule 5.3.4 Minimum 0.5% of the batch; minimum 12 unique increments of 1 g each, at least 50% homogenised for testing; primary, duplicate and replicate samples prepared and analysed separately. And maximum harvest batch package 25 lbs; "a licensed testing entity shall take a minimum of fifteen (15) sample increments of half a gram (0.5 g) each" for harvest-batch sampling. 0.5 g (harvest-batch sentence); 1 g (general sentence) — both sentences appear in Rule 5.3.4 as rendered; the relationship between them is [VERIFY] 15 × 0.5 g minimum for a harvest batch package (≤25 lbs)
Concentrates / extracts — Rule 5.3.6 Minimum 0.3% of the batch; enough samples to ensure homogeneity/consistency per the lab's accredited sampling policies 0.25 g per increment 1–2 lbs: 12; 2.01–3 lbs: 15; 3.01–4 lbs: 18; 4.01–10 lbs: 23; >10 lbs: 30
Infused / edible products — Rule 5.3.5 (production batch ≤150,000 units) Unit-count scale 1 packaged unit per increment ≤100 units: 3 (rendered "2 3"); 101–500: 6 (rendered "5 6"); 501–1,000: 9 (rendered "6 9"); 1,001–5,000: 12 (rendered "8 12"); 5,001–10,000: 15 (rendered "10 15"); 10,001–35,000: 20 (rendered "12 20"); 35,001–100,000: 30; 100,001–150,000: 50. The struck-through lower figures in the blackline are not adopted; the higher figure in each pair is the operative minimum as rendered [VERIFY against clean rule].
Raw or infused pre-rolls — Rule 5.3.7 (production batch ≤150,000 units) Unit-count scale; each increment = 1 packaged unit 1 packaged unit ≤50: 2; 51–100: 3; 101–500: 4; 501–1,500: 8; 1,501–3,000: 12; 3,001–10,000: 20; 10,001–35,000: 30; 35,001–150,000: 50
Inhalable concentrate products — Rule 5.3.8 (production batch ≤150,000 units) Same unit-count scale as pre-rolls; each increment = 1 packaged unit 1 packaged unit Same scale as pre-rolls (2 / 3 / 4 / 8 / 12 / 20 / 30 / 50)

Representativeness and integrity — Rules 5.3.3, 5.3.9, 5.3.10(A)–(D):

  • "Sampling of each harvest batch or production batch shall be conducted with representative samples such that there is assurance that all harvest or process lots are adequately assessed for contaminants and that the cannabinoid profile is consistent throughout" — Rule 5.3.3(B).
  • "A representative sample shall be taken from each container or area holding the harvest/production batch, from the top, middle, and bottom of the total contents" — Rule 5.3.3(D).
  • "For mandatory harvest/production batch sampling, the total batch weight or count to be sampled shall be verified by the testing licensee. A testing licensee shall not pull samples for mandatory testing if there is reasonable belief the full batch is not present for sampling" — Rule 5.3.3(C).
  • Sampling "shall be video-recorded, with the batch number stated verbally or in writing on the video at the beginning of the video and a visible time and date indication on the video recording footage. A facility employee must be present but not involved nor assisting with the sampling. The video recordings shall be maintained for 90 calendar days" — Rule 5.3.3(E). Note: this 90-day sampling-video retention is shorter than the 120-day general surveillance retention in §11.4; both figures are correct for their own subject matter.
  • A testing entity shall not: desiccate samples; test compliance samples without homogenisation where required; "[s]elect only the most desirable material from a batch or sample for testing"; or "[m]anipulate samples in any way that would alter the sample integrity or homogeneity of the sample. All sample increments must have the same genesis" — Rule 5.3.9.
  • The testing entity must have written sampling policies/procedures appropriate to the matrix; avoid contamination of non-sampled material; use sample containers "free of analytes of interest and appropriate for the analyses requested"; take sufficient sample for all requested tests plus lab QC; record the location of each sample/subsample; combine subsamples from the same batch into a single sample before testing; never combine subsamples/samples from different batches; never combine field duplicates with primary samples; assign field IDs unequivocally linked to lab IDs; assign a unique ID per test batch; maintain a documented identification system for samples, subsamples, preservations, containers, tests, extracts/digestates; durably mark each sample container with the lab's identification code; and enter a unique sample ID into lab records linking the sample to all lab activities — Rule 5.3.10(A)–(D).
  • Homogenisation: "All sample increments collected must be homogenized prior to sample analyses, notwithstanding foreign material testing" — Rule 5.4.1(A). Foreign-material testing is performed "on the total representative sample prior to sample homogenization" — Rule 5.4.10(C).

Chain of custody and transport of samples — Rules 5.3.10(E)–(N), 5.9:

  • Samples "shall be transported in one or more sealed containers and not be accessible while in transit" — Rule 5.3.10(E); the testing facility employee's vehicle "must [shall] not bear markings or other indication that it is carrying cannabis or a cannabis-infused product" — Rule 5.3.10(F); samples "shall be transported by a qualified employee of a licensed testing facility and shall not be transported in the same vehicle as other products" — Rule 5.3.10(G) (repeated at Rule 5.9.1: samples "shall not be transported in the same vehicle with any other usable cannabis or cannabis products").
  • After selection, both the establishment employee and the testing-facility employee "shall sign and date the chain of custody form, attesting to" product name, weight, correct identification in the seed-to-sale system, and (for a retest) that the testing facility "is not accepting a test sample that is prohibited from being retested" — Rule 5.3.10(J).
  • The establishment "shall enter in the statewide seed-to-sale system the test sample that is collected by a licensed testing facility, including the date and time the test sample is collected and transferred" — Rule 5.3.10(K).
  • Quarantine: "When a test sample is collected … that licensee shall quarantine the product that is undergoing the testing from any other product at the facility. The quarantined product may not be packaged, transferred, or sold until passing test results are entered into the statewide monitoring system" — Rule 5.3.10(L).
  • Samples "shall not be transferred or sold to any person or entity other than the licensee from whom the sample was collected", except a testing facility subcontracting safety tests to another testing facility — Rule 5.3.10(M). Additional sample material may be collected from the same licensee to complete required safety tests if Rule 5.3.10 is met — Rule 5.3.10(N).
  • Sample storage: the lab "shall store each test sample under the appropriate conditions to protect the physical and chemical integrity of the sample"; analysed samples are "appropriately segregated, controlled, and held in a controlled access area pending destruction or other disposal"; any undestroyed portion is either "[r]eturned to the licensed producer who provided the sample under chain of custody" or "[d]estroyed in accordance with the wastage disposal requirements" — Rule 5.3.11.
  • Transport manifests for samples: the testing entity must use an electronic inventory management system to create/maintain manifests; provide manifest copies to each originating and receiving establishment at change of possession; the originating copy must include licence number/business name/address/contact of the originator, complete inventory with weights/units and batch numbers, transport date and approximate departure time, printed names/signatures/ID-card numbers of testing personnel, and licence numbers/names/addresses/contacts of all end-point recipients; the receiving copy must include the same originator/recipient identification, delivered inventory with weights/units/batch numbers, date and estimated arrival time, accompanying personnel names/signatures/IDs, and printed names/titles/signatures of personnel accepting delivery; manifests must reflect complete chain of custody including storage instances, must not be altered after departure except to add the receiver's acceptance signatures, and must be retained by originator and receiver "for at least three (3) years from the date of receipt" — Rules 5.9.3–5.9.9. Testing entities transporting samples must also comply with Subpart 7 (transportation) — Rule 5.9.2.

Certificate of Analysis (COA) — Rule 5.7:

  • A COA is generated "for each representative sample"; it must contain "the results of all required analyses performed"; it must be uploaded into the seed-to-sale system "[w]ithin three (3) business day[s] of completing all analyses of a sample"; the testing entity "shall not release to any person any cumulative or individual test results prior to completing all analyses and providing the COA to the Department" — Rules 5.7.1–5.7.4.
  • Minimum COA contents (Rule 5.7.5): the term "Regulatory Compliance Testing" in ≥14-point font in the upper-right corner of each page (nothing above it); testing facility name/premises address/licence number; cultivator/processor/dispensary-distribution name/address/licence number as applicable; batch number (for pre-packaged product, the labelled batch number must match the COA batch number); sample ID information including matrix type and unique sample identifiers; sample history (dates collected, received, analysed, with results); a picture of the sample (for pre-packaged samples, an unobstructed image of the packaging); for dried flower, total batch weight in grams and total representative-sample weight in grams; for products/pre-rolls, total unit counts of representative sample and total batch; measurements; analytical methods, instrumentation, LOD and LOQ; a supervisory/management attestation that all required LQC samples were performed and met acceptance criteria; and analytes detected that are unknown, unidentified, or injurious if consumed, if any.
  • Reporting conventions (Rule 5.7.6): overall "pass" or "fail" for the entire batch; per-analyte and per-method "pass"/"fail"; below-LOQ reported as "<LOQ" (except cannabinoid results); not detected / below LOD reported as "ND"; tests not performed reported as "NT". The supervisory/management employee must validate, sign and date the COA — Rule 5.7.7; minor-error amendments may be requested and re-uploaded — Rule 5.7.8.
  • Tentatively identified compounds (TICs) (Rule 5.6): TICs are compounds detected by GC-MS that are not target residual-solvent analytes; the Department "may initiate an investigation" on a TICs report and "may require [the] cultivation facility or processing facility entity to submit samples for additional testing, including testing for analytes that are not required by these rules, at the … entity's expense."

11.1.5 Medical — failed tests, retesting, remediation, recalls, record duties

Reanalysis / resampling — Rule 5.5.1:

"If a sample fails any initial test, the cannabis testing facility entity that did the testing may reanalyze the sample. If the sample passes, another cannabis testing facility entity must [shall] resample the batch and confirm that result in order for the batch to pass testing."

General failed-batch rule — Rule 5.5.2:

"If a sample fails a test or a reanalysis under Rule [5.5.1], the batch: A. May be remediated or sterilized in accordance with this subchapter; or B. If it is not or cannot be remediated or sterilized under this rule, it [must] shall be destroyed in a manner specified by the Department."

Failed-test notice to a buyer — Rule 5.5.3:

"If a [c]ultivation facility entity or dispensary is permitted under this [Part] to sell or transfer a harvest batch that has failed a test, the [c]ultivation facility entity or dispensary must [shall] notify the processing entity [to] whom the harvest batch is sold or transferred of the failed test within twenty-four (24) hours of receipt of the COA."

By failure type:

Failure Remediation / sterilisation allowed? Retest requirement If remediation/sterilisation fails
Microbiological contaminants — Rule 5.5.4 Yes, by conversion: usable cannabis that fails may "be used to make a cannabinoid concentrate or extract if the processing method effectively sterilizes the batch, such as a method using a hydrocarbon-based solvent, or a CO2 closed loop system"; a concentrate/extract that fails may be further processed if the method effectively sterilises it on the same examples. Sterilised batch "must [shall] be sampled and tested in accordance with this Chapter and must be tested, if not otherwise required for that product, for microbiological contaminants, solvents and pesticides." "A batch that fails microbiological contaminant testing after undergoing a sterilization process … must [shall] be destroyed in a manner specified by the Department."
Solvents — Rule 5.5.5 Yes: "the batch may be remediated using procedures that would reduce the concentration of solvents to less than the action level." Remediated batch "must [shall] be sampled and tested … and must [shall] be tested if not otherwise required for that product … for solvents and pesticides." "A batch that fails solvent testing that is not remediated or that if remediated fails testing must [shall] be destroyed in a manner specified by the Department."
Water activity / moisture — Rule 5.5.6 Yes: the batch may "(1) Be used to make a cannabinoid concentrate or extract; or (2) Continue to dry or cure." A batch that undergoes additional drying/curing "must [shall] be sampled and tested in accordance with this [Part]." Not stated as a separate destruction sentence in 5.5.6; the general Rule 5.5.2 destruction rule and Rule 5.5.9 (below) apply.
Pesticides — Rule 5.5.7 No. "If a sample from a batch fails pesticide testing, the batch may not be remediated and must [shall] be destroyed in a manner permitted under this Part and/or approved by the Department and identified on the Department's website." N/A — destruction, not retest. —
Potency — Rule 5.5.8 Repackaging, not chemical remediation: "Usable medical cannabis that fails potency testing … may be repackaged in a manner that enables the item to meet the standard in Rule [5.4.6]." "Usable medical cannabis that is repackaged in accordance with this section must [shall] be sampled and tested in accordance with these Rules." General Rules 5.5.2 / 5.5.9 apply.
Any failure after remediation/sterilisation — Rule 5.5.9 Two-remediation cap: "A cannabis or cannabis product batch may only be remediated twice. If the batch fails after a second remediation attempt and the second retesting, the entire batch shall be destroyed in a manner approved by the Department." The facility "must [shall] inform a cannabis testing facility prior to samples being taken that the batch has failed a test and is being retested after undergoing remediation or sterilization." Destruction as stated.
Foreign material / homogeneity Foreign-material failure: batch "shall not be released for retail sale" (Rule 5.4.10(F)); no remediation pathway is stated in Rule 5.5 for foreign material — treat as [VERIFY] whether a foreign-material remediation pathway exists elsewhere in Part 22 or whether destruction is the only outcome. Homogeneity failure: product "shall not be released for retail sale" and all subsequent production batches of that item type undergo homogeneity testing "until three (3) consecutive batches pass" (Rule 5.4.11(D)). — —

Failed-remediation record duties — Rule 5.5.9(C): the cultivation or processing facility must "(1) Have detailed procedures for sterilization processes to remove microbiological contaminants and for reducing the concentration of solvents. (2) Document all sampling, testing, sterilization, remediation and destruction that are a result of failing a test under these rules."

Who orders a recall, how it is notified, and what the licensee must do — Rule 5.18 (MSDH) and Rule 11.1.1(H) (MSDH enforcement):

"The Department may issue public notice of a medical cannabis recall if, in its judgment, any particular cannabis and/or cannabis product presents a threat to the health and safety of qualifying patients. All medical cannabis establishments are responsible for complying with recall notices. Recalled items must [shall] be immediately pulled from production or inventory and held until such time as the Department determines the item is safe, may be remediated, or must [shall] be destroyed." — Rule 5.18.1.

Notes on the recall rule as read:

  • The Department (MSDH) is the recall-issuing authority in Rule 5.18; the rule does not in its text impose a separate licensee-initiated recall duty or a licensee-to-patient notification procedure. Any MDOR dispensary recall procedure, patient-notification template, or return-to-dispensary procedure, if one exists in Title 35 Part XI, was not located in the chapters read for this file [VERIFY — MDOR Chs. 28–29 (discipline/appeals) were indexed but their full text was not read line-by-line for this file].
  • The recall rule does not state a numeric deadline (hours/days) for pulling recalled items beyond "immediately", and does not state a record-retention period specific to recalls. The general record duties that would capture a recall are: batch-number records ≥2 years (Rule 5.2.4(A)); testing documentation ≥5 years (Rule 5.3.12); sample-transport manifests ≥3 years (Rule 5.9.8); and MDOR dispensary records for the current year plus three preceding calendar years (Title 35 Part XI, Ch. 25, as indexed in S-2).
  • MSDH's enforcement menu expressly includes "Recall cannabis and/or cannabis products" alongside fines, administrative holds, suspension, revocation, voluntary surrender, seizure/confiscation and destruction orders — Rule 11.1.1(A)–(I).
  • Administrative hold as the pre-recall tool (Rule 11.1.4): where MSDH has reasonable grounds to believe product is evidence of a violation or a threat to public health/safety, it may issue a written administrative-hold notice describing the product and the reasons; the product is identified in the seed-to-sale system; the licensee must "completely and physically segregate" it in a limited-access area, safeguard it, maintain the premises and comply with all security (surveillance/lock/alarm) requirements, and is "prohibited from selling, giving away, transferring, transporting or destroying" it except as authorised; MSDH "may lift the administrative hold or seek other appropriate relief" at any time. Voluntary surrender of held product is permitted only by the Department-authorised procedure.

11.1.7 Hemp — pre-harvest testing, DEA-registered labs and the 31 December 2026 delay, post-decarboxylation total THC, sampling agents, and finished-product testing

Governing programme. Because MDAC issues no hemp licences (S-7, quoted in §11.2.8), the governing hemp-testing rules for a Mississippi producer are the USDA Domestic Hemp Production Program rules at 7 CFR Part 990 (S-8), not a Mississippi testing rule. There is no Mississippi finished-product hemp testing rule located in this run (see final paragraph of this section).

Pre-harvest sampling — who, when, how (7 CFR § 990.24, verbatim in substance):

"USDA licensees must: (a) No more than 30 days prior to the anticipated harvest of cannabis plants, have a sampling agent collect samples from the cannabis plant for total delta-9 tetrahydrocannabinol concentration level testing. (b) Have samples collected from the flowering tops of the plant by cutting the top five to eight inches from the 'main stem' (that includes the leaves and flowers), 'terminal bud' (that occurs at the end of a stem), 'or 'central cola' (cut stem that could develop into a bud) of the flowering top of the plant. Sampling guidelines and training requirements for sampling agents are available from USDA. The method used for sampling must be sufficient at a confidence level of 95 percent that no more than one percent (1%) of the plants in the lot would exceed the acceptable hemp THC level. The method used for sampling must ensure that a representative sample is collected that represents a homogeneous composition of the lot. (c) Have an authorized representative of the USDA licensee present at the growing site during a scheduled sample collection, if possible. (d) Ensure that sampling agents are provided with complete and unrestricted access during business hours to all hemp and other cannabis plants, (whether growing or harvested), all hemp production and storage areas, all land, buildings, and other structures used for the cultivation, handling, and storage of all hemp and other cannabis plants, and all locations listed in the producer license. (e) Not harvest the cannabis crop prior to samples being taken. (f) Use post-harvest samples only for remediated biomass."

Who is a "sampling agent", and the producer-may-not-sample rule. Part 990's plan requirements ( § 990.3(a)(2), via S-9/USDA guidance) state that samples "must be collected by a sampling agent" and "[p]roducers may not collect samples from their own growing facilities." USDA maintains a directory of certified sampling agents qualified to sample USDA-licensed producers (USDA FAQ, S-9). The current USDA sampling-agent directory itself was not opened for this file [VERIFY if a Mississippi-specific sampler list is needed]; the rule requirement — a USDA-recognised sampling agent, not the producer — is the operative point.

After testing — harvest window and retest (7 CFR § 990.26):

"(a) The producer shall harvest the crop no later than thirty (30) days after the date of sample collection. (b) If the producer fails to complete harvest within thirty (30) days of sample collection, a second pre-harvest sample of the lot shall be required to be submitted for testing. (c) Harvested lots of hemp plants shall not be commingled with other harvested lots or other material. (d) Lots that meet the acceptable hemp THC level may enter the stream of commerce. (e) Lots that do not meet the acceptable hemp THC level are subject to § 990.27. (f) Any producer may request additional pre-harvest testing if it is believed that the original total delta-9 tetrahydrocannabinol concentration level test results were in error. Additional testing may be conducted by the laboratory that conducted the initial test, or another laboratory."

Post-decarboxylation total THC measurement (7 CFR § 990.25):

"Analytical testing for purposes of determining total THC in cannabis plants shall meet the standards in this section. (a) Laboratory quality assurance must ensure the validity and reliability of test results. (b) Analytical method selection, validation, and verification must ensure that the testing method used is appropriate (fit for purpose), and that the laboratory can successfully perform the testing. (c) The demonstration of testing validity must ensure consistent, accurate analytical performance. (d) Method performance specifications must ensure analytical tests are sufficiently sensitive for the purposes of the detectability requirements of this part. (e) Laboratory must have an effective disposal procedure for non-compliant samples that do not meet the requirements of this part. (f) Measurement of uncertainty (MU) must be estimated and reported with test results. Laboratories shall use appropriate, validated methods and procedures for all testing activities and evaluate measurement of uncertainty. (g) At a minimum, analytical testing of samples for total THC must use post-decarboxylation or other similarly reliable methods approved by the Secretary. The testing methodology must consider the potential conversion of THCA in hemp into THC and the test result must reflect the total available THC derived from the sum of the THC and THCA content. Testing methodologies meeting the requirements of this paragraph (g) include, but are not limited to, gas or liquid chromatography with detection. (1) The total THC shall be determined and reported on a dry weight basis. Additionally, measurement of uncertainty (MU) must be estimated and reported with test results. … (2) Any sample test result exceeding the acceptable hemp THC level shall be conclusive evidence that the lot represented by the sample is not in compliance with this part. (3) After December 31, 2022, USDA licensees may only use laboratories registered with the DEA to conduct testing under this section."

In plain terms: total THC = delta-9 THC + (THCA × 0.877) on a dry-weight basis (the 0.877 decarboxylation factor is the same factor MSDH uses for medical total THC at Rule 1.2.134), reported with measurement of uncertainty; a result above the acceptable hemp THC level, as adjusted by measurement of uncertainty, is conclusive non-compliance for that lot. The "acceptable hemp THC level" in Part 990 is 0.3% total THC on a dry-weight basis (see § 990.1 definitions, via the Part 990 text).

DEA-registered lab requirement and its delay — read carefully, because three dates are in play:

  1. CFR text as printed: § 990.25(g)(3) says "After December 31, 2022, USDA licensees may only use laboratories registered with the DEA to conduct testing under this section." That is the unamended CFR sentence.
  2. USDA enforcement practice as stated in the USDA FAQ (S-9): "Hemp testing laboratories must be registered with DEA to test hemp for compliance by December 31, 2025. On November 14, 2024, USDA extended the deadline for DEA registration, which had been January 1, 2025." The FAQ therefore already shows USDA exercising enforcement discretion past the CFR's 2022 date.
  3. Given federal baseline for this commission (fixed, not re-researched): "USDA enforcement of DEA-registered lab testing for hemp delayed to 31 December 2026." Adopted: through 31 December 2026, USDA enforcement of the DEA-registration requirement is delayed; the underlying testing, sampling, reporting, licensing, disposal/remediation and other Part 990 duties are not delayed. A Mississippi USDA licensee must still use a laboratory permitted by its licensing programme (USDA) and should verify with USDA where its hemp may be tested before choosing a lab, because programme-specific laboratory requirements can differ even during enforcement discretion. The December 2025 USDA extension notice itself was not opened as a standalone document for this file; the 31 December 2026 date is taken from the given baseline [VERIFY against the USDA notice if a filing depends on the exact scope of the delay].

Non-compliant hemp — disposal / remediation (7 CFR § 990.27, cross-referenced to the waste/cultivation side in §§11.2–11.3):

"(a) Cannabis plants exceeding the acceptable hemp THC level constitute marijuana, a schedule I controlled substance under the Controlled Substances Act (CSA), 21 U.S.C. 801 et seq., and producers must either use a DEA-registered reverse distributor or law enforcement to dispose of non-compliant plants or ensure the disposal of such cannabis plant on site at the farm or hemp production facility. (b) Producers must notify USDA of their intent to dispose of or remediate non-conforming plants and verify disposal or remediation by submitting required documentation. (c) If a producer elects to perform remediation activities, an additional sampling and testing of the post-remediated crop must occur to determine THC concentration levels."

Note the terminology tension: § 990.27(a) still calls over-limit plants "marijuana, a schedule I controlled substance". Under the given federal baseline, state-licensed medical marijuana is Schedule III from 28 April 2026; that baseline does not change the Part 990 hemp-disposal mechanics for a USDA hemp licensee, and § 990.27's Schedule I label should not be read as a statement about the medical programme. Flagged here so the two regimes are not conflated.

Finished-product hemp testing in Mississippi — absence of a rule:

  • No Mississippi finished-product hemp testing rule was located. MDAC issues no hemp licences and publishes no hemp-product testing rule (S-7). Run 1 located no hemp-derived product permit, age, testing, labelling or beverage statute. Nothing opened for this file changes that.
  • Consequence: for hemp, the only compliance testing regime located for a Mississippi producer is the pre-harvest Part 990 regime above (sampling agent + lab total-THC test + measurement of uncertainty + harvest window). There is no located Mississippi rule requiring finished hemp products (flower, extracts, edibles, beverages) sold in Mississippi to pass pesticides, heavy-metals, microbials, mycotoxins, solvents or potency testing, and no located Mississippi finished-product action levels. Any finished-product testing a Mississippi hemp business performs is therefore voluntary, buyer-driven, or driven by another jurisdiction's law — not by a located Mississippi hemp testing rule. This absence is itself a major gap and is carried to the summary.
  • Interaction with the post-11 December 2026 baseline: after 11 December 2026, the federal total-THC hemp definition and 0.4 mg total THC per container cap (given baseline) will apply at the federal level. No Mississippi statute or rule implementing, delaying, or adding to that cap was located in this run [UNAVAILABLE — no Mississippi response to PL 119-37 / PL 119-103 located, consistent with Run 1]. Whether Mississippi will enforce the federal cap through existing law, new law, or the AG-opinion theory (intoxicating hemp outside the medical programme as prohibited) is [VERIFY] and is outside §§11.1–11.4.

11.2 LICENCE RULES (medical, then hemp)

11.2.1 Medical — term, renewal timing, and the renewal certificate

MSDH licensees (cultivation, processing, testing, transport, disposal, research) — Rules 3.7–3.8:

  • Term: "Regular licenses issued by the Department under this Part are valid for one year from the date of issuance" — Rule 3.7.1. Renewal is annual — Rule 3.8.1.
  • Notice: "The Department shall send notification to each licensee of the duty to renew at [no] later than sixty (60) days prior to the expiration date of an active license. Notification will be to the email address [of] the primary contact person designated by the licensee on its application or latest renewal, as applicable" — Rule 3.8.2.
  • Filing window: the renewal application must be submitted "within thirty (30) days prior to the expiration date on the license" — Rule 3.8.3(A)(1).
  • Renewal contents (Rule 3.8.3(A)(1)(a)–(f), as applicable): (a) copy of current Certificate of Good Standing from the Mississippi Secretary of State's Office; (b) new, updated or revised service agreements; (c) any new or updated Standard Operating Procedures; (d) updated and/or revised diagram of the licensee's premises; (e) copy of licensee's current insurance policy; (f) updated vehicle information (transportation and disposal licensees). Plus: (A)(2) the licensee "continues to meet all the requirements of this Part"; (A)(3) proof it "remains in compliance with all requisite local permits and licenses"; (A)(4) the renewal fee "as required in Rule 3.2.2".
  • Department discretion: "Before renewing a license, the Department may require further information and documentation and may conduct additional background checks to determine that the licensee continues to meet the requirements of this Part" — Rule 3.8.3(B).
  • Material changes: "At the time of renewal, the licensee shall ensure that all material changes to the required plans and/or standard operating procedures have been communicated in writing to the Department" — Rule 3.8.4.
  • Inspection: "An annual inspection by the Department within sixty (60) days prior to expiration of a license issued under this Part may be required at the Department's discretion for renewal of the license" — Rule 3.8.5.
  • Non-renewal consequence: "A licensee whose license is not renewed shall cease all operations immediately upon expiration of the license, schedule a close out inspection with the Department, and destroy all cannabis and cannabis products in the licensee's possession in a manner approved by the Department" — Rule 3.8.3(C). And generally: "If the license of a medical cannabis establishment expires (by date), isn't renewed, or is suspended or revoked, operations … must cease as instructed by the Department" — Rule 3.8.8.

MDOR dispensaries — Title 35 Part XI, Ch. 04:

  • "Active licenses must be renewed on an annual basis. Licenses are valid for one year from the date of issuance. At the time of renewal, the licensee must demonstrate continued compliance with all applicable licensing criteria" — Ch. 04 ¶100.
  • "An annual inspection by the Department may be required for the renewal of the license" — Ch. 04 ¶101.
  • At renewal the licensee "shall ensure that all material changes to the required plans have been communicated in writing to the Department" — Ch. 04 ¶103; and "shall submit proof, through a renewed local authorization certification form, that the licensee is still in compliance with all requisite local permits and licenses and is in good standing with the municipality or other local entity wherein the licensee's facility is located" — Ch. 04 ¶104.
  • "An applicant may appeal a renewal denial as provided by law" — Ch. 04 ¶105; the renewal fee "must be paid by credit card or ACH debit through the licensing vendor selected for the Mississippi Medical Cannabis Program" — Ch. 04 ¶106.
  • Statutory renewal-certificate timing (§ 41-137-35(18), via S-10): "The MDOR and MDOH shall issue a renewal registration certificate within ten (10) days of receipt of the prescribed renewal application and renewal fee from a medical cannabis establishment if its license is not under suspension and has not been revoked." Verify against the official Code text [VERIFY] — this sentence is taken from a reproduction, and its interaction with the MSDH/MDOR discretionary inspection and background-check provisions above (which could extend a renewal in practice) is not spelled out in either regulation.

Work permits (context for licence rules, Run 1 baseline confirmed): a work permit "shall be valid for five (5) years from the date of issuance" — MSDH Rule 3.11.4; it "shall not be transferable to others [non-transferrable]" and is "the property of the [permitted] individual" — Rule 3.11.5; name changes must be notified in writing "within ten (10) business days" with a new application as specified — Rule 3.11.6. Work-permit holders must hold a permit before working for, volunteering at, or maintaining a ≥10% ownership interest (direct or indirect) in an MSDH- or MDOR-licensed establishment — Rule 3.11.1.

11.2.2 Medical — transfers and sales of licences / businesses, and ownership changes

Statutory anchor (§ 41-137-35 / Act § 24, via S-10 and the SB 2095 text): "No license issued by the MDOH, MDOR or MDAC shall be transferred by the license holder to any other person or entity except with the written consent of the applicable licensing agency." The MSDH and MDOR regulations implement that consent requirement in parallel, near-identical chapters. There is no "licence sale" as a standalone transferable asset in either regulation: what is transferred is an ownership interest in the licensed entity, with prior agency approval. An asset sale that changes the licensed entity's owners without approval is a violation (see revocation trigger below).

MSDH — Rule 3.10 (all MSDH licensees):

"A licensee may transfer ownership interests, including without limitation partial ownership, only after the application for a transfer of an ownership interest has been approved by the Department." — Rule 3.10.1.

Application requirements — Rule 3.10.2: the application must (A) "[b]e completed on forms and/or a system made available by the Department"; (B) "[b]e submitted to the Department"; and (C) "[c]ontain all required supplemental information provided by the person or entity seeking to assume an ownership interest, similar to that which is required in an application for a cannabis cultivation license, to demonstrate compliance with all applicable requirements for licensure, including but not limited to fingerprinting and background check requirements."

Sanction for unapproved transfer — Rule 3.10.3: "The Department may revoke or suspend a license upon discovery of any effort or attempt to transfer an ownership interest in a license without complying with the requirements of this Part."

Threshold question — is there a de minimis transfer that needs no approval? On the text read, no. Rule 3.10.1 covers "ownership interests, including without limitation partial ownership" without a percentage floor. The 10% figure that appears elsewhere in the programme is not a transfer-approval threshold; it is (i) the work-permit trigger (≥10% direct/indirect ownership requires a work permit — Rule 3.11.1), (ii) the disclosure threshold (licensing agencies "shall require disclosure only of persons, entities or affiliated entities who directly or indirectly own ten percent (10%) or more" — § 41-137-35(19), via S-10), and (iii) the ownership-cap measure (see §11.2.3). A transfer of any ownership interest, even below 10%, therefore requires prior MSDH approval on the face of Rule 3.10.1. Any MSDH practice of waiving approval for small transfers, if one exists, was not located in the text read [VERIFY with MSDH before relying on a de minimis theory].

Testing facilities — additional transfer contents (Rule 3.10.4): see §11.1.3 for the full list (legal name; principal officers/board members; truth attestation; owner + technical laboratory director signatures with dates; per-owner no-excluded-felony attestation; per-owner no-relationship/no-interest attestation covering dispensaries, cultivation, processing, transport, disposal and research entities; non-diversion pledge; age-21 verification for principal officers/board members). The testing-facility independence rule means a transfer that would create a prohibited relationship must fail.

MDOR dispensaries — Title 35 Part XI, Ch. 05 (near-identical):

"A licensee may transfer ownership interests, including without limitation partial ownership, only after the application for a transfer of an ownership interest has been approved by the Department." — Ch. 05 ¶100.

Application — Ch. 05 ¶101: (1) on Department forms; (2) submitted to the Department; (3) "accompanied by all required forms and supplemental information, provided by the person or entity seeking to assume an ownership interest, similar to that required in an application for a dispensary license to demonstrate compliance with all applicable requirements for licensure." Criminal-history checks: "Criminal history record checks are required for anyone proposed as an owner, officer, director, board member, or anyone with an economic interest" — Ch. 05 ¶102. Unapproved-transfer sanction: "The Department may revoke or suspend a license upon discovery of any effort to transfer an ownership interest in a license without complying with the requirements of this subsection" — Ch. 05 ¶103.

Death / disability — MDOR temporary appointee (Ch. 06), a transfer-adjacent rule with no MSDH parallel located in this file:

"Ownership or operations generally may not be transferred to a person or business entity prior to the approval of an application for transfer of ownership interests. However, in case of death or physical or mental disability of any licensee, the estate, trustee, or guardianship of the licensee shall be allowed to operate the permitted business for a period not exceeding sixty (60) days after the death or disability. During the sixty (60) day period, any member of the licensee's immediate family may make an application to the Department for the unexpired portion of the license of the decedent to be assigned to him." — Ch. 06 ¶100. "If such application is approved, the applicant shall be granted the right, without payment of an additional permit fee, to operate the licensed place of business for the unexpired portion of the time of the original license." — Ch. 06 ¶101.

Whether MSDH has an equivalent estate/guardianship operating window for cultivation/processing/testing licensees was not located in the MSDH text read [VERIFY]. Do not assume the MDOR 60-day rule applies to MSDH licensees.

Management agreements (dispensaries) — a related control on de facto transfer: "No management agreement for a licensed place of business shall be effective until the Department has approved the same including review of all economic interests created by such management agreements" — MDOR Ch. 18 ¶104; the agreement "must provide that the licensee will be absolutely responsible for any and all violations … occurring on the licensed premises" — Ch. 18 ¶105; and except for a management agreement creating no economic interest for the operator, "the licensee in all cases must operate the business for himself and have direct control over its operation" — Ch. 18 ¶103. The MDOR "economic interest" definition (Ch. 01 ¶108) excludes flat-fee lenders, flat-monthly-rate or <10%-of-gross-revenue management operators, non-controlling investments (e.g. mutual funds), and flat-rate landlords — see §11.2.3.

11.2.3 Medical — ownership caps (reconciled)

Adopted rule (all three official texts agree): a person may not hold a direct or indirect ownership or economic interest of greater than 10% in more than one (1) cultivation facility licence, more than one (1) processing facility licence, and more than five (5) dispensary licences.

  • MSDH renewal bar — Rule 3.8.6(D): a licence "may be suspended, revoked, or [shall] not be renewed … if … [r]enewal will result in any person having a direct or indirect ownership or economic interest of greater than ten percent 10% in more than one (1) Mississippi cannabis cultivation facility entity license; more than one (1) Mississippi cannabis processing facility entity license; and more than five (5) Mississippi cannabis dispensary licenses."
  • MDOR definition — Ch. 01 ¶106: "An entity or individual cannot have greater than a ten percent (10%) interest in more than five (5) dispensaries."
  • MDOR renewal bar — Ch. 04 ¶102(3): a licence shall not be renewed if "[r]enewal will result in any person having a direct or indirect ownership or economic interest of greater than ten percent (10%) in more than five (5) dispensary licenses."
  • Statutory disclosure threshold — § 41-137-35(19) (via S-10): "A licensing agency shall require disclosure only of persons, entities or affiliated entities who directly or indirectly own ten percent (10%) or more of a medical cannabis establishment issued a license by the licensing agency."

Reconciliation notes:

  1. "5", not "4". The secondary "4 dispensaries" figure is wrong; it is contradicted by the MSDH rule, the MDOR definition and the MDOR renewal rule. Adopted: 5.
  2. "Greater than 10%" vs "10% or more". The cap uses "greater than ten percent (10%)" (so exactly 10% does not itself breach the cap), while the disclosure duty uses "ten percent (10%) or more" (so exactly 10% must be disclosed). The work-permit duty uses "ten percent (10%) or greater" (Rule 3.11.1). These are three different thresholds for three different duties; do not collapse them.
  3. Scope gaps [VERIFY]: the MSDH renewal bar as rendered lists cultivation, processing and dispensary caps but does not in that paragraph state caps for testing, transport, disposal or research licences. Whether a person may hold >10% in multiple testing/transport/disposal licences is not answered by Rule 3.8.6(D) as read; the testing-facility independence attestation (Rule 3.10.4(E)(2)) is a different, stricter rule (no relationship/interest at all in another establishment type for testing-facility owners). Any multi-licence structure involving a testing facility must be checked against Rule 3.10.4, not just the 1/1/5 cap.
  4. Affiliates / indirect interests count: both MSDH and MDOR rules say "direct or indirect" ownership or economic interest. The MDOR economic-interest definition (Ch. 01 ¶108) is the operative definition for dispensaries: sole proprietor, partner, member holding ≥10% equity/similar interest, stockholder owning ≥10% of available stock, or any interest entitling the holder to regular payments based on a percentage of revenue from cannabis-product sales in any licensed dispensary — with the four exclusions listed in §11.2.2 above.

11.2.4 Medical — renewal bars (grounds on which renewal must / may be refused)

MSDH — Rule 3.8.6: a licence "may be suspended, revoked, or [shall] not be renewed" if: (A) outstanding fines are owed to the Department; (B) an owner has been convicted of a disqualifying felony; (C) the establishment "has not engaged in licensed activity at the licensed premises for a period of one (1) year or more", unless it submits evidence of reasonable justification "including without limitation death, illness, natural disaster, or other circumstances beyond the medical cannabis establishment's control"; (D) renewal would breach the 1/1/5 ownership cap (see §11.2.3); (E) the entity owes delinquent taxes (an entity on an agreed payment plan that it is following "are not considered to be delinquent"); (F) the entity "no longer meets all eligibility requirements for the issuance of a [medical cannabis establishment] license"; (G) the entity "does not meet regulatory requirements set by the Department"; and/or (H) the entity "provides [misleading, incorrect, false or fraudulent] information". Separately, renewal "may be denied after consideration … of the licensee's demonstrated history of violations of these [rules]. The number and severity of violations will be considered" — Rule 3.8.7.

MDOR dispensaries — Ch. 04 ¶102: a licence "shall not be renewed" if: (1) outstanding fines are owed to the Department; (2) an owner or individual with an economic interest has been convicted of a disqualifying felony; (3) renewal would breach the >10%-in-more-than-5-dispensaries cap; (4) the entity owes delinquent taxes; or (5) the entity "no longer meets all eligibility requirements for the issuance of a dispensary permit."

Dispensary construction deadline as a renewal-adjacent trap (statute, via S-10): § 41-137-35(17): "If a dispensary license is issued to an applicant that is still constructing the licensed premises, the applicant must complete construction and fulfill all obligations required by the Department of Revenue to open for business within eighteen (18) months, or the license shall be revoked." Note the tension with older secondary summaries that said 12 months (the proposed-regulation summary in 2022); the statute as reproduced says 18 months. Verify against the official Code [VERIFY] before advising a dispensary on a construction timeline.

11.2.5 Medical — surrender, suspension, revocation: grounds and process

Surrender / termination — MSDH Rule 3.9 (voluntary surrender, abandonment, or cessation for any reason, including revocation):

"Licensees who permanently abandon the licensed premises or otherwise permanently cease all activities relating to the operation of a medical cannabis establishment under its license, whether a result of revocation, voluntary surrender or other reasons, shall follow the following procedures for terminating the license: A. Provide written notice of abandoning the licensed premises or ceasing operations at least forty-eight (48) hours in advance to the Department stating the reason for surrender of the license; name(s) and contact information of the person(s) responsible for closing of all business operations; and the address where business records will be retained. B. Provide the Department with a full accounting of all cannabis plants, cannabis and cannabis products located within the licensed premises; and C. Destroy all cannabis plants, cannabis and cannabis products in its possession as instructed by the Department."

And: "The annual licensing fee paid at the time of application is non-refundable. No portion of the annual licensing fee shall be returned to the licensee" — Rule 3.9, final sentence. Voluntary surrender is also an express enforcement-menu item: the Department may "[a]ccept the voluntary surrender of a license" and "[a]ccept the voluntary surrender of cannabis plants, cannabis and/or cannabis products" — Rule 11.1.1(E), (I).

Whether MDOR has a parallel dispensary surrender procedure in Title 35 Part XI was not located in the chapters read [VERIFY — Chs. 28–29 (discipline/appeals) may contain it; their full text was not read line-by-line for this file]. Do not assume Rule 3.9's 48-hour notice procedure applies to dispensaries.

Suspension / revocation grounds — MSDH Rule 11.1:

  • General ground: the Department may act "in any case in which it finds that [a] licensee has failed to comply with the requirements established by the Mississippi Medical Cannabis Act and/or the rules, regulations or standards promulgated in furtherance of such act" — Rule 11.1.1. Available actions, alone or in combination: monetary penalties; administrative hold; suspension; revocation; voluntary surrender (licence and/or product); confiscation/seizure; destruction orders; recall (see §11.1.5).
  • Disciplinary schedule: "The following schedule of disciplinary actions included as APPENDIX B to this Part shall be used when administratively disciplining medical cannabis establishments" — Rule 11.1.1, final paragraph; "The Department reserves the right to increase penalties based on aggravating circumstances and/or the medical cannabis establishment's history of violations and corrective actions." Appendix B's per-violation fine table was not reproduced in the rendered text read, except for one line located by search: "recall of product $5,000 [per] [e]ach directive from the Department regarding recall" [VERIFY — Appendix B in full].
  • Suspension cap and effect: "the Department may suspend the license of a medical cannabis establishment if necessary to protect public health, safety, or welfare. A suspension shall not exceed a period longer than six (6) months. A medical cannabis establishment may continue to possess and cultivate cannabis as otherwise authorized to do so under its license during a suspension, but it may not dispense, transfer or sell cannabis" — Rule 11.1.2. (The statute as reproduced in secondary summaries states the same six-month cap and the same possess/cultivate-but-not-dispense/transfer/sell effect; the rule text is the authority cited here.)
  • Seizure / hold / destruction triggers — Rule 11.1.3: the Department may "seize, destroy, confiscate or place an administrative hold on any cannabis plants, cannabis and/or cannabis products" where, among other cases: (A) failure to log and/or tag in the seed-to-sale system; (B) alteration of product in a manner that fails to comply with Part 22; (C) failure to package and label per Part 22; (D) cultivation/harvest/manufacture/transfer in a non-compliant manner or form; or (E) improper use, handling, storage, transport, transfer or other possession.
  • Specific revocation triggers located in the text read (in addition to the general Rule 11.1.1 ground): unapproved ownership transfer (Rule 3.10.3; MDOR Ch. 05 ¶103); non-renewal grounds in Rule 3.8.6 (which are framed as "suspended, revoked, or [shall] not be renewed"); testing-facility record falsification / non-compliance (Rule 5.4.14, "immediate disciplinary action, including sanctions, fines, or both"); failure to satisfy construction conditions if a licence was granted on uncompleted construction (MDOR Ch. 02 ¶101(5): failure to satisfy conditions "may be cause for revocation or denial of renewal", and deviation from submitted construction plans that would have disqualified the applicant is prohibited); failure to modify a withdrawn dispensary security plan within 30 days (MDOR Ch. 08 ¶102, see §11.4.2); and the statutory 18-month dispensary construction deadline (§ 41-137-35(17), see §11.2.4).

Process — notice, hearing, appeal (MSDH Rules 11.1.5–11.1.6):

  • Notice: "At the time of denial of an application for licensure or the imposition of any monetary penalty and prior to imposition of non-monetary sanctions, suspension or revocation of a license, written notice of the contemplated action shall be given to the applicant or licensee at the address on record with the licensing agency. Such notice shall [specify] the reason(s) for the proposed action and shall notify the licensee of the right to a hearing on the matter." Initial notice is by "personal delivery, or mailing by certified mail, signature required, or by electronic mail to the applicant or licensee, to the medical cannabis licensee at the address on record" — Rule 11.1.5.
  • Appeal/hearing: MSDH "will provide to a licensee/aggrieved party an opportunity for a prompt and fair appeal process" for fines/penalties/sanctions, denial, suspension or revocation — Rule 11.1.6. "Upon written request by the licensee/aggrieved party and within twenty (20) days of receipt of the initial notice of administrative action, the licensee/aggrieved party may file a request for an appeal which is handled through the means of an administrative hearing with the Department. Once [requested], the State Health Officer shall be notified … and shall appoint a qualified Hearing Officer within thirty (30) days to set a date, time and place for the administrative hearing convenient for all parties." Failure to appeal within the prescribed time makes the decision "final and cannot be further appealed".
